design.source: EIA Form 861 (2024), Sales to Ultimate Customers, normalized by the eia_861 adapter
design.aggregation: revenue-weighted average residential price = sum(residential revenue) / sum(residential sales) * 100, cents/kWh
design.rows: observed (Data Type = O), all service types (bundled + energy + delivery)
design.tva_area_definition: utilities whose Balancing Authority code = TVA

uncertainty.note: Population aggregates from the EIA-861 census of utilities; no sampling variance. Ownership comparison is observational, not causal.

literature.author: Kwoka, John
literature.title: The comparative advantage of public ownership: evidence from U.S. electric utilities
literature.journal: Canadian Journal of Economics / Revue canadienne d'economique
literature.finding: While privately owned systems achieve lower costs in generation, public systems generally have an advantage in the end-user-oriented distribution function with its more non-contractible quality attributes (published abstract; the paper's specific coefficients are paywalled and not reproduced here).

benchmark.name: Computed EIA-861 US residential average vs official EIA Electric Power Monthly 2024 annual average (Table 5.3)
benchmark.official_source: EIA Electric Power Monthly, Table 5.3, 2024 annual, Residential = 16.48 cents/kWh
